summary: Marker-scanning loop that classifies a marker byte relative to a reference counter a2 and dispatches decoder states through a sub-object vtable. Initializes dispatcher state to 117 and current marker from this[94]; each iteration classifies the marker into category 1 (expected marker, break), 2 (skip and read next), or 3 (acceptable stop, return). On category 1, this[94] is reset to 0.

operations.description: Write dispatcher state fields: obj+0x14 (+0x14) = 117, obj+0x18 (+0x18) = v3, obj+0x1C (+0x1C) = a2.
Dispatch through obj vtable entry +0x4 (obj = *a1, this+0x0) with argument -1.

Marker classification: v3 < 192 gives category 2 (skip); v3 outside 208-215 or equal to ((a2+1)&7)+208 or ((a2+2)&7)+208 gives category 3; v3 equal to ((a2-1)&7)+208 or ((a2-2)&7)+208 gives category 2; otherwise category 1 (expected marker).
Per iteration write dispatcher state: obj+0x14 (+0x14) = 96, obj+0x18 (+0x18) = v3, obj+0x1C (+0x1C) = category v5.
Dispatch through obj vtable entry +0x4 with argument 4.
Category 1: expected marker found, loop breaks.
Category 2: call BitstreamTokenReader(a1) to read the next marker; if it returns false, return 0.
Re-read marker v3 = a1[94] (+0x178) after skipping the token.
After the expected marker is found, reset a1[94] (+0x178) to 0 and return 1.

unresolved: Semantics of the dispatched states 117 (initial) and 96 (per-iteration) and the dispatch arguments -1 and 4 are not established by the evidence.
The a2 reference-counter arithmetic and the meaning of the 208..215 marker range are DERIVED from the raw branch structure only.
Role of this+0x0 (pointer to the dispatcher object) is a DERIVED reading from the raw dereferences.
Category 2 (skip) is interpreted as an unexpected or out-of-range marker without independent confirmation.
